snapshot.text: Flughafen Wien, the Vienna airport group, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} in FY2024, and the complete repayment of interest-bearing financial liabilities leaves it with net cash of {{net_cash@FY2024}}.
The EBITDA margin was broadly unchanged at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, while net leverage moved further into net cash territory, down by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}}.
The point to watch is cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}.

credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}.
Total debt was stable at {{total_debt@FY2024}}, so gross leverage held at {{gross_leverage@FY2024}} and net cash rose by {{net_cash.change@FY2024}} to {{net_cash@FY2024}}.

FFO grew by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}}, but free cash flow declined by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, but traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} was well below the {{traffic_growth.change@FY2024}} slower than in FY2023.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger increased by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2024}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}}, helped by the temporary inflation-linked adjustment of airport charges.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments rose by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue up by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}.

With total debt of {{total_debt@FY2024}} against that cash, the group holds net cash of {{net_cash@FY2024}}, and the repayment of interest-bearing liabilities has greatly reduced its exposure to interest rate changes.
A financing commitment was given for the City Air Terminal joint venture's new train sets, part of which was drawn as a loan in the year.

peer_positioning.text: Flughafen Wien has the lowest net leverage of the airport group ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}), at {{net_leverage@FY2024}} against a peer median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2024}}, and also ranks first on gross leverage.

Cash liquidity to revenue is the strongest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2024}}), at {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} against a median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2024}}.

The group sits in the middle of the peer group on EBITDA margin and capex intensity, while traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} is the weakest of the group ({{traffic_growth.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, in line with the peer median.
Traffic: growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} is below the peer median of {{traffic_growth.peer_median@FY2024}} and the weakest of the group ({{traffic_growth.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

Regulation: airport charges are temporarily adjusted by average inflation, a rule that ends at the end of 2026, so aeronautical revenue per passenger of {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}} depends on the tariff formula that follows.
Litigation: disputes with the Maltese government and employee claims concerning Malta International Airport remain outstanding, which the group considers unfounded.
